25                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 


                                                                2490

 1   Resolution Number 2049, by Senator Little, 

 2   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

 3   proclaim May 10-17, 2015, as Fibromyalgia 

 4   Awareness Week in the State of New York.

 5                "WHEREAS, An estimated 10 million 

 6   people in the United States and an estimated 3 to 

 7   6 percent of the world's population --

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Can I 

 9   have some order in the chamber, please.

10                The Secretary will continue.

11                THE SECRETARY:   "WHEREAS, An 

12   estimated 10 million people in the United States, 

13   and an estimated 3 to 6 percent of the world's  

14   population, have been diagnosed with 

15   fibromyalgia, an illness for which there is yet 

16   no known cause or cure; and 

17                "WHEREAS, A chronic syndrome that is 

18   increasing at alarming rates, fibromyalgia causes 

19   debilitating widespread pain and fatigue, appears 

20   to have a genetic component, and occurs in women, 

21   men, and children of all ethnicities; and 

22                "WHEREAS, Patients with fibromyalgia 

23   often have to learn to live with widespread pain 

24   throughout their bodies, extreme fatigue, sleep 

25   disorders, stiffness and weakness, migraine 


                                                                2491

 1   headaches, numbness and tingling, and impairment 

 2   of memory and concentration; and 

 3                "WHEREAS, It often takes an average 

 4   of five years to receive a diagnosis of 

 5   fibromyalgia, and medical professionals 

 6   frequently are inadequately educated regarding 

 7   the diagnosis and treatment of fibromyalgia; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, A 2007 study found that 

 9   fibromyalgia patients spend between $100 and 

10   $1,000 per month above insurance costs to see 

11   healthcare providers; costs in the United States 

12   are estimated between $12 and 14 billion per 

13   year, and account for the loss of 1 to 2 percent 

14   of the nation's productivity; and 

15                "WHEREAS, According to a survey of 

16   1,168 fibromyalgia patients, 25 percent had 

17   received disability payments, and total  

18   healthcare costs may be two to three times  

19   higher than patients without fibromyalgia; 

20   failure to diagnose and adequately treat 

21   fibromyalgia has deep financial implications for 

22   patients and for the healthcare system; and 

23                "WHEREAS, According to a fact sheet 

24   provided by the National Fibromyalgia 

25   Association, 90 percent of physicians agree there 


                                                                2492

 1   is a need for more physician-oriented 

 2   information, and 82 percent of physicians agree 

 3   that fibromyalgia is difficult to treat with 

 4   currently available tools; use of complementary 

 5   and alternative medicine is two and a half times 

 6   higher in fibromyalgia patients; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, Increased awareness and 

 8   expanded knowledge of the realities of life with 

 9   fibromyalgia will allow the community at large to 

10   better support people who struggle with the 

11   challenges of this chronic pain disorder; and 

12                "WHEREAS, A nonprofit charitable  

13   organization, the National Fibromyalgia and 

14   Chronic Pain Association has joined together with  

15   other groups around the country, including the 

16   International Institute for Human Empowerment, 

17   Inc., based in New York State, to promote 

18   fibromyalgia awareness and support, including 

19   improved education, diagnosis, research and 

20   treatment; and 

21                "WHEREAS, The International 

22   Institute for Human Empowerment, Inc., a 

23   nonprofit organization in the Capital District of 

24   New York, is the sponsor of various fibromyalgia 

25   awareness events, as well as the Select 


                                                                2493

 1   Empowerment Seminar report:  'Fibromyalgia: 

 2   Awareness, Advocacy, and Action,' encouraging the 

 3   medical community, patients, employers, 

 4   government health and human rights agencies, 

 5   educators, and caregivers to work together to  

 6   support and improve the lives of fibromyalgia 

 7   patients; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, The International 

 9   Institute for Human Empowerment, through the 

10   leadership of its founder and executive director 

11   Sue Shipe, Ph.D., recently initiated a 

12   Fibromyalgia Task Force with the stated 

13   intentions to secure support for a new edition of  

14   'Fibromyalgia:  Awareness, Advocacy and Action,' 

15   of which 5,000 reports have already bee 

16   distributed locally, nationally, and 

17   internationally; to create a scholarship for 

18   fibromyalgia patients to access complementary  

19   therapies which are not covered by insurance; and 

20   to provide continued public conferences regarding 

21   new research findings regarding fibromyalgia; and 

22                "WHEREAS, To address the concern 

23   that the average time to fibromyalgia diagnosis 

24   is five years, the Fibromyalgia Task Force will 

25   provide legislative awareness and seek 


                                                                2494

 1   legislative action to improve physician education  

 2   by supporting medical schools in New York State 

 3   to provide fibromyalgia education for physicians; 

 4   and 

 5                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body 

 6   recognizes the generous efforts of two of its 

 7   outstanding citizens on behalf of fibromyalgia 

 8   patients residing in New York State:  Dorota L. 

 9   Hausner-Sypek, M.D., of the Center for 

10   Rheumatology, Bone and Joint Center, Albany, 

11   New York, supports many patients with 

12   fibromyalgia and other rheumatic illnesses, and 

13   collaborates with the International Institute for 

14   Human Empowerment in distributing to patients and 

15   other physicians copies of the report 

16   'Fibromyalgia:  Awareness, Advocacy and Action'; 

17   she has spoken at and has been a resource for 

18   fibromyalgia conferences in the Capital District 

19   of New York; and 

20                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body 

21   recognizes the critical work of Social Security  

22   Disability Attorney Ira Mendleson, III,  Esq.,  

23   of Buckley, Mendleson, Criscione and Quinn, P.C., 

24   of Albany, New York, for providing outstanding 

25   service to fibromyalgia patients; Mr. Mendleson 


                                                                2495

 1   presented at the Select Empowerment Seminar on 

 2   fibromyalgia in regard to the application process 

 3   for Social Security Disability, contributed an 

 4   expert article for the report 'Fibromyalgia: 

 5   Awareness, Advocacy and action,' and has 

 6   presented at fibromyalgia conferences in the 

 7   Capital District of New York; Mr. Mendleson is 

 8   also a valuable resource on the Fibromyalgia Task 

 9   Force of the International Institute for Human 

10   Empowerment; and 

11                "WHEREAS, The work of Dorota L.  

12   Hausner-Sypek, M.D., and Ira Mendleson, III, 

13   Esq., is greatly valued, especially by those 

14   patients whose lives, families and careers have 

15   been disrupted by fibromyalgia; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Medical research in the 

17   Capital District of New York is making 

18   significant progress in the area of fibromyalgia 

19   and chronic pain, and deserves the support of the 

20   people of New York; and 

21                "WHEREAS, The community's focus on 

22   fibromyalgia and its impact on patients' lives 

23   will help guarantee hope for a better future for 

24   people with fibromyalgia; and 

25                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body 


                                                                2496

 1   recognizes the needs of those chronically ill 

 2   people who suffer from fibromyalgia, and urges 

 3   all of our citizens to support the search for a 

 4   cure and assist those individuals and families 

 5   who deal with this devastating syndrome on a 

 6   daily basis; now, therefore, be it 

 7                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 8   Body pause in its deliberations to memorialize 

 9   Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to proclaim May 10-17,  

10   2015, as Fibromyalgia Awareness Week in the State 

11   of New York; and be it further 

12                "RESOLVED, That copies of this 

13   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

14   the Honorable Andrew M. Cuomo, Governor of the  

15   State of New York; the International Institute 

16   for Human Empowerment, Inc.; the Center for 

17   Rheumatology, Bone and Joint Center, Albany, 

18   New York; and Buckley, Mendleson, Criscione and 

19   Quinn, P.C., Albany, New York."

20                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Can I

24   Mr. President.

25                Each year it is my privilege to ask 


                                                                2497

 1   the body of this Senate to pass a resolution for 

 2   a Fibromyalgia Week so that more and more people 

 3   will become aware of what fibromyalgia is and the 

 4   devastating effects it has on those who are 

 5   afflicted with it.

 6                Women represent more than 75 percent 

 7   of those who are affected with fibromyalgia, 

 8   although it can affect children and men as well.  

 9   And every patient presents differently, which 

10   makes diagnosis a real challenge.  Sometimes --

11                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Excuse 

12   me, Senator Little.

13                I'm going to ask one more time, 

14   please.  I know there's a lot of activity in the 

15   chamber right now.  But if you can take 

16   conversations outside the chamber so we can hear 

17   the members.  It's very difficult for the 

18   stenographer to hear right now.  So please, if we 

19   can take those conversations outside the chamber.

20                Senator Little, please continue.

21                SENATOR LITTLE:   As I said, 

22   fibromyalgia presents itself differently in every 

23   single patient, making it very difficult to 

24   diagnose.  In some cases it is a primary disease, 

25   in others may be secondary to lupus, rheumatoid 


                                                                2498

 1   arthritis or even cancer.  

 2                But fibromyalgia patients also have 

 3   a very unique set of problems, because 

 4   fibromyalgia is not well known and the research 

 5   is not really accepted as well in medical 

 6   schools.  Many doctors are not even aware of what 

 7   fibromyalgia can do.  

 8                So it can take a long time, many 

 9   years, for someone to actually finally be 

10   diagnosed with fibromyalgia.  Unfortunately, in 

11   the meantime, patients often lose their jobs, 

12   their financial independence, and unfortunately 

13   even their spouses.

14                Treatment of fibromyalgia includes 

15   medication to relieve symptoms, exercise as 

16   tolerated, lifestyle changes to remove stress and 

17   improve sleep quality, improved diet, and many 

18   complementary therapies.  

19                The disorder can be seen in 

20   families, among siblings, among parents and 

21   children, and it can affect and usually affects 

22   people between the ages of 20 and 50 years old.  

23                Delay of the diagnosis, as you can 

24   imagine, can cause the person a lot of 

25   discomfort, pain and expense.  It also allows the 


                                                                2499

 1   illness to progress, too often to the level of 

 2   absolute disability.

 3                I really want to thank the Governor 

 4   for proclaiming this in previous years and doing 

 5   so this year, because awareness is so important, 

 6   as well as advocacy.  

 7                And we are joined today by several 

 8   people who are advocates for making fibromyalgia 

 9   better known and to improve research.  And these 

10   are people who are right here in our Albany area.  

11   We have with us Dr. Hausner, Ira Mendleson, III, 

12   and Sue Shipe, all from the Fibromyalgia Task 

13   Force.  We're fortunate that the Albany Medical 

14   Center is very involved in the research of 

15   fibromyalgia.  

16                And I appreciate them for coming 

17   today and ask all of you to join me in this 

18   resolution.

19                Thank you.

 1   Zhang Qiyue, who has just taken over the position

25   visit our chambers here and to be in the State

11                I rise today to acknowledge an 

12   important event in my district, the Juneteenth 

13   40th Anniversary Gala this Friday, May 15th, and 

14   to recognize those who have been committed to 

15   carrying on a celebrated tradition, the 

16   Juneteenth Festival of Buffalo for 40 years.  

17                It's a tradition I've been honored 

18   to participate in for several years.  Started in 

19   1976 by the Juneteenth Festival of Buffalo, Inc., 

20   then known as B.U.I.L.D., the festival was 

21   created to celebrate a culturally relevant 

22   alternative to the country's bicentennial 

23   celebration as well as celebrate the ending of 

24   the Civil War and the freedom for all slaves in 

25   the United States.


                                                                2508

 1                For 40 years the members of this 

 2   nonprofit organization staffed entirely by 

 3   volunteers have made extraordinary contributions 

 4   to our community.  Committed to promoting the 

 5   history of African-American heritage through 

 6   educational and cultural activities, the 

 7   Juneteenth Festival of Buffalo, Inc., organizes 

 8   one of the largest annual parades in the City of 

 9   Buffalo Brook and by far one of my favorites to 

10   march in.  

11                After having outgrown the original 

12   location on Jefferson Avenue, the parade now 

13   marches down Genesee Street to an audience of 

14   thousands.  It gets bigger and bigger every 

15   single year.  The parade culminates in Martin 

16   Luther King, Jr., Park, where hundreds of vendors 

17   gather to sell ethnic foods and wares, live music 

18   is played, and families spanning generations come 

19   together to take part in the entertainment.  

20                The members and volunteers of this 

21   wonderful organization should be commended for 

22   their hard work and tremendous dedication to our 

23   community in hosting this event that's gaining 

24   greater and greater magnitude every single year.  

25                I'm honored to have the opportunity
